newsitem.title: USA: Dow hits another high, 10th so far this month.
newsitem.headline: Dow hits another high, 10th so far this month.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average jumped to yet another record Wednesday -- its 10th so far this month -- in a rally driven by gains in the shares of General Motors, Caterpillar and Boeing.
The 30-share index rose 32.42 points to 6,430.02, beating Tuesday's record of 6,397.60.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,350 to 1,068 on active volume of 489 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"There's no question it's frothy but this is sustainable as long as bond yields stay to the market's advantage," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury added 11/32, or $3.44 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.41 percent from 6.44 percent on Tuesday. Bonds got a boost from a successful auction of $12.5 billion of five-year U.S. notes, traders said.
"If you made a model of what drives the stock market you'd have to say none of the variables is changing except bond yields," Battipaglia said.

While several broader market gauges again hit records -- among them the NYSE composite index and the Standard & Poor's 500 index -- the Dow again outperformed the broader market, extending a trend that has raised yellow warning flags on Wall Street.
Among them was Prime Charter Ltd.'s Chief Investment Strategist Scott Bleier, who reduced the amount of stocks and bonds in his firm's asset allocation model, citing the recent run-up in prices.
"We feel that the activity in the first-tier, largest capitalised names has reached frenetic levels," he said.
Despite mounting caution, investors were still buying any blue chip stock that appeared poised to outperform other issues.
Caterpillar was one such stock, surging 4-3/4 to 78-3/4 after Smith Barney upgraded its opinion of the heavy machinery giant.

"There's so much money still waiting to get in on any reason," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist Van Kampen American Capital. "Any move from a hold to a buy has the potential to move a stock like this."
Boeing Co. climbed 2-3/8 to 96-3/8 on published reports that American Airlines was set to place a multi-billion aircraft order.

American parent AMR, which declined to comment on the reports, lost one to 91. After the close of trading, the union representing American Airlines' pilots said its board approved a tentative labour pact with the company. AMR has long maintained it would not buy any aircraft until reaching such a labour agreement.

General Motors rose 2-1/2 to 57-1/8 on rumours that its Hughes Electonics Corp. unit might merge with Raytheon Co. Hughes, whose stock trades separately from GM, jumped 3-3/4 to 53-1/2 and Raytheon gained 2-1/2 to 52-3/8. All three companies declined to comment on the rumours.
Revlon Inc. fell 3-1/2 to 30-1/8 after Smith Barney trimmed its fiscal 1997 earnings estimate on the company.
IBM, which helped propel the Dow index the last few days, fell 1-1/2 to 152-5/8 on profit taking after rallying to a 52-week high of 159 early in the session.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 2.32 points to 1,264.94.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks gained 1.79 to 743.95, a record. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.55 to 587.19.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks was up 1.00 at 392.80, a record. The average share added 11 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,174.852, up 20.961 or 0.29 percent.
